correctness.rationale: For exact quadratic oracle q(u)=uᵀHu, the calibrated M(u)=d q(u)((d+2)uuᵀ−I)/2 is unbiased by spherical fourth moments. Directly computing E[q(u)q(v)] over distinct Haar columns yields ((d+1)t²−2s)/(d(d−1)(d+2)). Hence the centered Frobenius cross-covariance is C=[(−d²+2d+4)/(2(d−1)(d+2))]s−[d(d+1)(d+4)/(4(d−1)(d+2))]t²; risk difference is (k−1)C/k. Sign: d=2 iff t²/s<2/9 and d=3 iff <1/42 for worse frame; d>=4 always improvement. PSD H has t²>=s and improves. Independent exact 2D integration of H=diag(1,−1) gives iid risk 3/2 versus orth risk 2. Equalities checked; no claim about nonquadratic/noisy oracle.
